limitations: These are source-level predictions only. No v5 RED, v6 GREEN, fixture, Git command, launcher, received helper or probe was executed.

The shared guard intentionally uses common v5/v6 fields. It does not independently validate the complete metadata schema, record HEAD format, launch-specific cwd/hash, or the v6-only deadline flag. The pinned source producers, no-overwrite entry checks and branch-specific postcheck constraints supply the relevant relationships.

The l30 v6 rejection filter at 985-986 uses substring membership and at least one allowlist phrase rather than an exact structured problem count/category. An invented additional diagnostic containing the same key would satisfy that predicate. No concrete unrelated failure emitted by the pinned fixture/launcher path was found that exploits this while all other guard requirements hold; this is recorded as a boundary of the string-based filter, not a blocking finding.

The l29 expected source mismatch filter uses repr(rewritten) membership rather than an exact message equality, but pinned v5 source code necessarily emits its effective-source mismatch when the required raw rewritten get_url is present. The exactly-one-problem constraint excludes simultaneous emitted failures.
